title: A dial built from two prompts
allegory: A steering vector is a dial built from two recordings: run the model on 'Love' and on 'Hate', subtract what it was computing in each, and you get an arrow from hate toward love that you can add into any new prompt, turned up or down, to shift its tone with no training at all.
map: two recordings of the model's inner state, one per word
cached residual streams for a contrast pair, such as 'Love' and 'Hate', at one layer
subtracting one recording from the other
the steering vector: the activation difference, which cancels what the two prompts share
turning the dial up or down
the coefficient: +5 at layer 6 in the original post, ±8 in ARENA's template
slipping the arrow into a new conversation at its very start
adding the vector at the prompt's first positions; KV caching carries it into every generated token
the two recordings must line up word for word
contrast prompts need equal token length and aligned positions, or the difference is mostly padding noise
where_else: Contrastive steering vectors in [4.1]: the same recipe aimed at misalignment, with its own trap

hamming.what: The difference between a model's activations on two contrasting prompts, added into the residual stream of a new prompt to push its behaviour one way.
hamming.when: When you want a behavioural knob between prompt engineering and fine-tuning: cheap, gradient-free and applied at run time, as in turning 'I hate you because' affectionate.
hamming.why: Two forward passes and a subtraction gave a usable control knob with no optimisation at all, though layer and coefficient have no principled derivation, so sweep them and check the effect is robust.
